doc: This is wild. Arresting people just for posting their opinions on social media is a massive red flag for any country that claims to be a democracy. The “liking posts” part is what makes this feel extra insane. Like even before you get to the politics, arresting people for basic social media activity is not something a democracy should be normalizing. how do they even track that? are cops just scrolling through likes all day?

The gross part is how addiction suddenly becomes a sacred moral issue or a punchline depending entirely on whose last name is attached. Hunter Biden isn’t an elected official, but half of Congress talks about him like he’s chairing Ways and Means. Yep. The tell is that the people yelling the loudest about Hunter’s addiction almost never pivot to treatment access, fentanyl policy, drug courts, anything practical. It’s just tabloid politics with a committee gavel.

This is exactly where the vague language starts to feel useless. If the number is even close to right, then the basic demand is stop bombing places full of kids, let aid in, and quit treating civilian deaths like a PR problem. It is honestly sickening how the world can just watch thousands of kids die and treat it like some political debate instead of an immediate emergency. Right, and it’s the basicness of it that matters. Not organizing an attack, not leaking military info, just liking or sharing something about Gaza and suddenly the police are involved. That is not some tiny wartime exception, that is the state training people to shut up. Exactly, it's a terrifying slippery slope when just liking a post can get you locked up.

Yeah but calling it “global indifference” makes it sound like nobody knows. People know. The issue is governments are treating dead kids as a PR problem instead of a red line. Yeah the free speech branding gets pretty thin when liking the wrong Gaza post can put police on your doorstep. People can argue about the exact cases, but the direction of it is ugly. Yeah, that’s the bit people keep trying to make binary. Being horrified by Oct 7 doesn’t mean you have to pretend police visits over Gaza posts are normal democracy stuff. It really does feel like nuance has completely died. If you don't 100% align with one side's narrative, both sides end up hating you.

It's absolutely heartbreaking. How can the world just watch this happen and do nothing to stop it? Exactly. If they actually cared about addiction, they'd be talking about policy, not using one guy's struggle as a political prop. It's insane how much of a meat grinder that war has become, yet people act like it's just a stalemate where nothing happens. It's wild how a flag can mean completely different things to different people depending on who is holding it.

“Urgent attention” is doing a lot of work here. If the number is even close to right, then say the concrete part: stop bombing areas full of kids, get aid in, and stop treating dead children like a PR problem. Yeah, this is the part people wave away until it is their side getting hauled in for a like or a share. You can support Israeli civilians and still admit the state cracking down on Gaza speech is ugly as hell.

The bit that gets me is how quickly the numbers become background noise. People argue about wording while the actual children are dead, missing, or being pulled out of rubble. Calling for action is fine, but at minimum that means a ceasefire and letting aid in properly, not another round of diplomatic throat-clearing. The sheer scale of what's happening to kids there is horrifying. We can't just keep looking at these numbers like they're some abstract data points instead of actual lives. Exactly. The annoying bit is watching people treat civil liberties like a nice-weather hobby. If the state can send police after people for a like or a share, that’s not some tiny wartime footnote, it’s the whole free speech claim falling apart in real time. Honestly, it feels like nuance died a long time ago on the internet. If you don't 100% agree with one side's extreme, you're immediately labeled the enemy by both.

“Urgent attention” is the easy part. The harder part is admitting what it actually requires: stop the bombing, open aid routes, and quit acting like dead kids are just an unfortunate footnote to the operation. Exactly. Pretty hard to sell the 'beacon of freedom' angle when the state is literally policing double-taps on social media.
